passages.scripture: We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.

lines.text: We who are strong must help the weak.
We who are strong must carry the burdens of those who are not strong.
We who are strong must not seek to please ourselves.

passages.scripture: Each of us should please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.

lines.text: Each of us must act for the good of our neighbor.
We must seek to build up our neighbor.
We must not focus only on ourselves.
We must help others grow and become stronger.
We do help others by doing what is good for them.

passages.scripture: For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”

lines.text: Christ did not seek to please Himself.
Scripture says this about Christ.
The insults of those who insult God fell on Christ.

passages.scripture: For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.

lines.text: God gave us the Scriptures in the past.
Everything written in the Scriptures teaches us.
The Old Testament Scriptures written in the past need to be taught correctly.
Scriptures give us instruction.
We learn from the Scriptures.
We gain endurance through the Scriptures.
The Scriptures encourage us.
The Scriptures help us have hope.

passages.scripture: Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus, so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

lines.text: God gives endurance.
God gives encouragement.
Paul prays that God will help us think the same way toward each other.
We must do this because we belong to Christ Jesus.
When we are united in mind and voice, we can glorify God.
God is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

passages.scripture: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.

lines.text: Christ accepted us.
Christ did this to bring glory to God.
Therefore, we accept one another.
When we accept one another, we also bring glory to God.

passages.scripture: For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the circumcised on behalf of God’s truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs, so that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written: “Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing hymns to Your name.”

lines.text: Christ became a servant to the circumcised.
The circumcised are the Jews.
Christ served them for the sake of God’s truth.
The patriarchs are the ancestors of the Jewish people.
God made promises to the patriarchs.
Christ did this to confirm the promises God made to the patriarchs.
Christ also acted so that the Gentiles may glorify God.
The Gentiles are all other nations besides the Jews.
The Gentiles glorify God because of God's mercy.
As David says in Scripture: “Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles.”
David also says in Scripture: “I will sing hymns to Your name.”
This Scripture prophesied praises to God and the word of God being given to the Gentiles.
The actions of Christ leading to Gentiles glorifying God was a fulfillment of this Scripture.

passages.scripture: Again, it says: “Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.”

lines.text: God calls the Gentiles to rejoice.
God calls the Gentiles to join the people of God in joy.
The Scriptures say this in Deuteronomy.

passages.scripture: And again: “Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples.”

lines.text: All Gentiles must praise the Lord.
All peoples must glorify God.
This is written in Psalms in the Scriptures.

passages.scripture: And once more, Isaiah says: “The Root of Jesse will appear, One who will arise to rule over the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will put their hope.”

lines.text: Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah spoke about the future.
Isaiah said, “The Root of Jesse will appear.”
Jesse was the father of King David.
The Root of Jesse means a Descendant from Jesse’s family.
This Descendant will come.
This Descendant will rise up to rule over the Gentiles.
The Gentiles are all the nations who are not Jews.
The Gentiles will put their hope in this Descendant.
This Descendant is the One in whom the nations trust.

passages.scripture: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe in Him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

lines.text: God gives hope.
God can fill us with joy.
God can fill us with peace.
We receive joy and peace as we believe in God.
God wants us to overflow with hope.
By the power of the Holy Spirit we overflow with hope.

passages.scripture: I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.

lines.text: Paul writes to his brothers.
Paul is convinced his brothers are full of goodness.
Paul is convinced his brothers are filled with all knowledge.
Paul is convinced his brothers are able to instruct one another.

passages.scripture: However, I have written you a bold reminder on some points, because of the grace God has given me to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

lines.text: God gave Paul grace.
God made Paul a minister of Christ Jesus.
God sent Paul to serve the Gentiles.
Paul served by sharing the gospel of God.
The service of Paul is a priestly service.
Paul wrote to these Romans boldly on some points.
Paul wanted to remind these Romans.
Paul served so that the Gentiles may become an offering to God.
God accepts this offering of the Gentiles.
The Holy Spirit makes this offering of the Gentiles holy.

passages.scripture: Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.

lines.text: Paul rejoices in Christ Jesus.
Paul serves God.
In Paul's service, Paul rejoices in Christ Jesus.

passages.scripture: I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed, by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.

lines.text: Paul will not speak about anything except what Christ has done through Paul.
Paul will only speak about what Christ has done through Paul.
Christ has worked through Paul to lead the Gentiles to obey God.
Christ has done this through Paul's words and actions.
Christ has shown His power through signs and wonders.
Christ has worked by the power of the Spirit of God.
Paul fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.
Paul fully proclaimed Christ from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum.

passages.scripture: In this way I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.

lines.text: Paul wants to preach the gospel.
If Paul preached in places where another apostle already started a church, then Paul would have been building on someone else's foundation.
Paul did not want to build on someone else’s foundation.
Paul did not preach where someone else started a church before him.
Paul did not preach where Christ is already known.
Paul chose places to preach where the gospel had not yet reached.
Paul preached the gospel where people did not yet know Christ.

passages.scripture: Rather, as it is written: “Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”

lines.text: Some people have not been told about God.
These people will see God.
Some people have not heard about God.
These people will understand.
Paul says this to quote from the Scriptures in Isaiah.

passages.scripture: That is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.

lines.text: Paul wanted to come to the believers in Rome.
But Paul often could not come to the believers in Rome.
Paul was hindered many times from coming to the believers in Rome.
Paul preaching the gospel in places that did not yet have the gospel kept Paul away from coming to Rome.

passages.scripture: But now that there are no further opportunities for me in these regions, and since I have longed for many years to visit you, I hope to see you on my way to Spain. And after I have enjoyed your company for a while, you can equip me for my journey.

lines.text: There were regions where Paul had been ministering with the gospel.
Paul had finished his work in these regions.
There were no more opportunities for Paul to serve in these regions.
Paul had wanted to visit the believers in Rome for many years.
Paul hoped to see the believers in Rome as Paul traveled to Spain.
Paul wanted to spend some time with the believers in Rome.
Paul hoped they will help him on his journey to Spain after he visits them.

passages.scripture: Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there.

lines.text: Paul was traveling to Jerusalem.
Paul planned to serve the saints in Jerusalem.
The saints are the believers in Jerusalem.
Paul’s purpose is to help the believers in Jerusalem.

passages.scripture: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.

lines.text: Macedonia and Achaia are Christian regions.
The Christians in Achaia and Macedonia decided to help others.
The Christians in Macedonia and Achaia wanted to give a gift.
There were poor believers in Jerusalem.
The Christians in Macedonia and Achaia chose to help these poor Christians.
Macedonia and Achaia were happy to help the Christians in Jerusalem.

passages.scripture: They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they are obligated to minister to them with material blessings.

lines.text: As Jesus is a Jew, it is through the Jews that salvation and spiritual blessings came to the Gentiles.
As Gentiles share in the spiritual blessings of Jews, so Gentiles are obligated to share their material blessings with the Jews.
The believers in Macedonia and Achaia were Gentiles.
The believers in Macedonia and Achaia were obligated to give this help to the saints in Jerusalem.
And although the believers in Macedonia and Achaia obligated to help, but they were pleased to give a gift to the poor saints in Jerusalem.

passages.scripture: So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.

lines.text: Paul serves the saints in Jerusalem.
Paul collected a gift to give to the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
Paul plans to finish this service by delivering the gift.
Paul will make sure the saints in Jerusalem receive this gift.
After Paul completes this service, he plans to travel to Spain.
Paul will go to Spain by way of the believers in Rome.

passages.scripture: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.

lines.text: Paul knows he will come to the believers in Rome.
Paul will bring the full blessing of Christ when Paul comes to Rome.

passages.scripture: Now I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me.

lines.text: Paul urges his brothers, the believers in Rome, to help Paul.
Paul urges the believers in Rome by the Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul also urges his brothers by the love of the Spirit.
Paul asks his brothers to join Paul in his struggle.
Paul asks the believers in Rome to pray to God for Paul.

passages.scripture: Pray that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints there, so that by God’s will I may come to you with joy and together with you be refreshed.

lines.text: Paul asks the believers in Rome to pray for Paul.
Paul wants God to deliver Paul from the unbelievers in Judea.
Paul wants his service in Jerusalem to be acceptable to the saints there.
Paul desires to joyfully come to the believers in Rome.
Paul wants to visit the believers in Rome by the will of God.
Paul hopes to be refreshed together with the believers in Rome.
Paul requests that the believers in Rome pray for all this.

passages.scripture: The God of peace be with all of you. Amen.

lines.text: God is the God of peace.
God is with all of us.
Amen.
